claims: L3Harris connects propulsion, sensing, electronic warfare and space systems to missile-defense replenishment, counter-UAS and allied defense needs; current causal leverage is industrial capacity and qualified production, not merely award volume.
Capacity expansion can relieve propulsion/sensor bottlenecks, but successor constraints shift toward suppliers, skilled labor, appropriations and program integration.
causalEdges: defense threat/replenishment demand -> appropriations/contracts -> propulsion/sensor production -> fielded defense capacity -> protection/deterrence need
supplier/labor availability -> production ramp -> delivery reliability
substitutes: other qualified defense primes and propulsion suppliers
counterfactuals: If appropriations or named programs slow, diversified space/EW/counter-UAS exposure can cushion but not eliminate government-demand concentration.

claims: Large awards and order counts are not equivalent to realized revenue or margin; undefinitized/framework awards preserve pricing and timing uncertainty.
Simultaneous capacity programs create execution and supplier risk, while government concentration exposes timing to appropriations and procurement decisions.
unknowns: margin profile on newly awarded production
supplier constraint severity across propulsion/sensor programs
improvementPaths: show capacity milestones translating into deliveries
definitize major awards without adverse economics
demonstrate supplier and labor throughput resilience
falsifiers: sustained on-time delivery and stable/improving margins through the ramp would materially weaken execution-risk concerns
